## Symptoms

### ReleaseOrchestrator executions fail at ApplyAppConfig
**Description:** In account 012345678901_1 (us-east-1), every recent ssm-baseline-m4-*-ReleaseOrchestrator execution failed because its child ApplyAppConfig automation failed: aebf62ab (r1-a14, 2026-11-25 03:46), cdd22328 (r2-a14, 05:34), 5f5732bd (r3-a14, 07:18). **Time:** 2026-11-14T13:28:55Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: /etc/app/app.conf missing on target instance
**Description:** The file /etc/app/app.conf does not exist on i-1234567890abcdef0_47 (ip-10-0-0-6.ec2.internal), account 012345678901_1, us-east-1. The ApplyAppConfig AWS-RunShellScript step checks for the file and exits 3 when it is missing. Run Command 00000000-0000-4000-8000-9c09aa25f432 failed at 07:18:50Z. That failed child ApplyAppConfig 00000000-0000-4000-8000-5ec9f0350679, which then failed parent ReleaseOrchestrator 00000000-0000-4000-8000-a6cfcc6a3c07 (started 07:18:43Z). The same error appears in every failed child run (11-14 and three on 11-25). The runbooks themselves work as written. The requested execution 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab could not be found, so this cause applies to the matching runs and only most likely to the requested one.

# Mitigation Summary

## Action
No mitigation action can be identified.

## Reasoning
The fix would be to restore /etc/app/app.conf on i-1234567890abcdef0_47 and re-run the orchestrator, but nothing is left to apply it to. The instance is gone from EC2 and SSM (the only running instances, i-1234567890abcdef0_3, i-1234567890abcdef0_4 and i-1234567890abcdef0_5 in stack obsgap-poc-workload, are not the target). The ApplyAppConfig and ReleaseOrchestrator documents have been deleted, and execution 0123abcd-0123-4567-89ab-0123456789ab does not exist. If these runbooks are recreated against a new host, they will fail the same way unless that host gets /etc/app/app.conf first. The prevention requirements are below.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Provision /etc/app/app.conf on every instance a release targets, before the release runs
**Description:** Create the file during instance provisioning (launch template user data, a State Manager association, or configuration management) so a fresh or replaced instance never reaches a release without it. Get the correct contents from the application owner.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A newly launched target instance has /etc/app/app.conf before any ReleaseOrchestrator run
- An ApplyAppConfig run against a freshly provisioned instance completes with ResponseCode 0 and prints 'configuration applied'

#### 2. Have the ReleaseOrchestrator runbook check its target before starting the nested ApplyAppConfig step, and report failures clearly
**Description:** Before the executeAutomation step, add a pre-flight step that confirms the target is SSM-managed (PingStatus Online) and that /etc/app/app.conf exists. If either check fails, stop with a clear error naming the instance and the file.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- If the file is missing, the orchestrator fails at the pre-flight step with an error that names the instance ID and the file path
- If the target instance is not SSM-managed or not Online, the run is rejected before ApplyAppConfig starts

#### 3. Keep a record of release command output and runbook versions
**Description:** Turn on CloudWatch Logs or S3 output for the Run Command steps, and keep the ReleaseOrchestrator and ApplyAppConfig documents under version control instead of deleting them after use.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- stdout and stderr from every ApplyAppConfig run can be found in CloudWatch Logs or S3 after the run
- The runbook versions used by any past execution can be found after the run
